_comment: Explicit exceptions to the local clock-gating rules (tools/check-cg.py, docs/rtl-coding-style.md 'Local clock gating'), written by the module's owner. One entry per module, rule (CG-1, CG-2, CG-3, CG-4, CG-5 or RST-1) and register: module, rule, target, why, by, date. why says what was measured and why the rule cannot or should not be met. A CG-5 waiver also carries ports, the input ports it lets into the enable, and enable_ngd, the enable's total depth: the latest port's arrival plus the cone, within CCV_NGD_CG_EN (OI-59). A waiver carries its threshold and fails again past it (Daniel; OA's response OI-66): a CG-3 waiver states floor_pct and measured_pct, each by scenario (idle, medium, high), the floor 2 points under the measurement and never over it, and optionally enable, the one gate of its register it takes, by its enable's name as check-cg reports it (OI-66); an allowance waiver, for CG-1's registers written every cycle or CG-4's ungated flops, states max_flops and measured_flops. A waiver of flops that hold an interface lead signal, any rule, carries lead: true, and one of flops that capture a credit-return pulse carries credit: true; their flops count against the block's 2% per instance (Daniel's rulings on RI-15 and RI-14, 2026-11-06, RA revs 87 and 88; RI-17). A waiver that excuses nothing is refused; one beside a ratchet entry supersedes it.

waivers.why: OA's response OI-58: a timer's grant has no lead (the grant register's D is select's pick at 24.3 NGD, and the issue loop cannot pay a cycle). The grant comes from ooe_sched's third (* keep *) copy of its grant register (grant_w_cq04h), for this module alone, at 1 NGD (ooe_wake.ngd.json; OA's response re:OI-122, rev 375). Under C9h the hint match is decoded from the raw capture inside the enable: check-cg measures each timer's enable cone at 6.1 NGD at worst, 7.1 in all with the grant's arrival, within CG-2's 8. Every other term of the enable is this module's own flops (OA's responses OI-58, OI-62).

OA's response OI-65 (OA tab, 2026-10-21, rev 156): the group of each slot's take, count and valid bits (14 flops) is clocked by rename's per-slot take-enable, deq_sel_cq01h (a superset of its take, from rename's flops at 2.0 NGD, ooe_decq.ngd.json; the superset is asserted, deq_sel_covers), or the slot's own transit, arrival and flush flops. check-cg measures the cone at 2.0 to 2.2 NGD, 4.2 in all with the arrival, within CG-2's 8. One enable shared by the slots gave 61 to 71% DCGE; per slot, 90% and over. It replaces OI-58's "some warp takes" waiver of about 5 (deq_any_cq01h, dropped).

DA's decision (a), OA's response OI-66 (OA tab revs 174-179): the fits, per slot 20 flops with its take-enable, are recomputed every cycle from decq's heads, rename's pool and floors, the ROB room and the allowances held. Each gate's enable is the slot's change bit, the OR of its producers' register enables (OA's rev 174: decq's arrivals, the ROB room, the pool and floors) and of its own takes, squash, restore edge, held allowances and rotation, each lead exact in the model's bench (no-dq-ev, no-rob-en, no-pool-en controls). Even with exact leads the fits change on only 61-68% of enabled cycles: a warp streaming with credits and room to spare keeps fits of all ones while its heads move (OI's rev 163, a bench-held attribution: 130,007 enabled slot-cycles, 80,859 changing). Measured at 8ef3dff: slot 0 64/61%, slot 1 64/63%, slot 2 64/68% (medium/high), slot 3 never enabled; idle enables none. This entry is slot 0's gate (its enable fits_en[0]), held to its own floor, 2 under its measure (OA's rev 181; check-cg's enable key, TI's cd901fd). Slot 3's gate is never enabled in the unit's scenarios and so needs none. With the writer prefix counts in the same gate (OI-67, 2026-10-23), measured 64 / 73% (medium / high); the floors stand.

DA's decision (a), OA's response OI-66 (OA tab rev 179): the allowances held (20 flops, one-hot per credit) are recomputed every cycle from rename's pool and floors and the warps with a head; enabled on any slot's change bit, they change on 66% (medium) and 54% (high) of enabled cycles, measured at 8ef3dff; idle enables none. Floors 2 under.

OA's rev 219 (OI-76): the names' pool registers (GPR and predicate, 10 flops) are formed from the remainders as they stand, less the older take, so they must be clocked while a names' take is registered and on the edge after the remainders move (nv), not with the counters alone; the bench holds every take to the model's and the scarce build's no-take-q2 control fails without the older take. They change on few of those cycles: the GPR pool stands at its saturation XM while names are plentiful, and the predicates' at the pool less its floors while no slot holds past its floor. Measured 12% (medium) and 24% (high); idle enables none. Clocked with the counters instead, under their enable or nv, the 175-flop gate fell to 68% in medium (96% high); skipping nv while both pools stand at XM leaves it there, the predicates' pool never reaching XM. Each pool alone would be a 5-flop gate, past the module's allowance (19 of its 23.9 flops in use). Floors 2 under the measure.

The candidates' rows and valids (72 flops), one gate: the valids clocked on the rows' enable, the reset among its terms (DA's grant, OA's direction, DA tab rev 94). OI-81 (a) and OI-82 (OA's revs 252-254; granted by DA, 2026-10-25): each slot's two home-position candidates, the lowest owned live row with its home section or home pair free, found over all 192 rows and registered. The find's result is stable while the section bits move under it, so the candidates change on few of the cycles a section changes; the only exact enable is the 192-row find itself, and no enable from the module's own flops within CCV_NGD_CG_EN reaches 75% (a per-slot enable, measured on the model, sees a candidate change on 17-20% of its events). Without them Rename 2 needs a per-lane find and a fourth rename stage (+1.7% mean, +9.2% worst on the OI-34 sweep). Home-only (8 candidates, not 24) costs nothing on the sweep. Idle enables none. Floors 2 under the measure.

MIU's kept lead, each slot's m_hi_cr02h, m_lo_cr02h and m_am_cr02h (46 flops, one gate a slot). Its predicate-write lead (phys_pred, active_mask) is on ccv_miu_rcu_data only in T-1 (RA-40: the payload's own fields, leading, not copies), and the write and the guard forward need it in T, so this module keeps it a cycle. Nothing earlier names the write, so the only enable is the lead's own valid & pred_we, straight from RCU's interface flop on the channel (DA's ruling on RI-11: a flop at every block boundary; rcu_pred.ngd.json, arrival 0): the enable starts at a flop and its cone is one AND, within CG-2's 8. Loaded every cycle instead, the 4 x 46 flops would be 184 ungated flops against this module's 2% (57). Allowed by Daniel's ruling on RI-15 (RA rev 87, DA rev 109, 2026-11-06): module-level CG waivers for interface lead signals, each lead flop charged to the RCU block's per-instance 2%, to fit at final construction.

R's guard lead kept for A, rg_hi_cr02h and rg_lo_cr02h (14 flops, one gate). lead_guard_pred (RA-31, RA-32, the split guard read) is on ccv_ooe_rcu_issue only in A-1, with R's valid, and is predecoded into these psel flops for A. The only enable is that valid, straight from RCU's interface flop (DA's ruling on RI-11; rcu_pred.ngd.json, arrival 0), a wire. Loaded every cycle instead, the 14 flops put the module one flop past its 2% (58 ungated against 57.4); a binary lead flop instead would put the decode on the branch path. Allowed by Daniel's ruling on RI-15 (RA rev 87, DA rev 109, 2026-11-06): module-level CG waivers for interface lead signals, each lead flop charged to the RCU block's per-instance 2%, to fit at final construction.

RCU's credit returns on its inbound fixed-rate channels (Done, kill and reset tab, Credits RCU returns): one flop a slot, its D the slot's valid on the wire, so the credit returns in the cycle the payload lands; 9 issue slots, 32 lane-result copies, 4 MIU data slots, 45 flops written every cycle. They are the channels' own control pulses, captured every cycle like any receiver's: a repeater's are charged to its block's budget, not its own allowance (Daniel, 2026-10-19), and these are the same pulses at the block's own end, about 0.02% of RCU's 246,000 flops. A gate cannot hold them: the only enable that names a return is the valid itself, an input (CG-5). The module's allowance (7) takes its other 6 single flops (reset, kill_v_q, done wake, idle, CSR responder). Daniel's ruling on RI-14 (RA rev 88, DA rev 110, 2026-11-06): credit-return pulse flops are charged to the receiving block's per-instance 2%, marked credit for check-cg (TI rev 344).

The kill drain counter (Done, kill and reset tab: kill_drain, loaded with KILL_DRAIN in K and counting to 0), 5 flops at KILL_DRAIN 16, its value at CCV_LAT_SFU 12 since Z (RA rev 95; 13 would still give 16), so max 5. Its enable is its own (kill_v_q or a nonzero count) and it changes on every enabled cycle, but 5 flops are under a gate's 8; a one-hot drain timer would make a gate of 16 to save 5. rcu_kill is the block's control residue, 60 flops (Partition tab), so its own allowance is the floor of 7: the reset, kill_v_q, the done wake, the idle flop, the CSR responder, kill_ack_q and its pending bit take it.

The kill ack epoch (CCV_P_W_KILL_EPOCH, 2 flops), loaded at K under kill_v_q (the tab's kill_ep_q and kill_ack_ep_q in one: the ack is low from K to ack-ready, so the ack epoch can take the epoch at K). Under a gate's 8, and nothing else shares its enable. rcu_kill is the block's control residue, 60 flops (Partition tab), so its own allowance is the floor of 7: the reset, kill_v_q, the done wake, the idle flop, the CSR responder, kill_ack_q and its pending bit take it.
